title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
This incident shows impersonation at scale, where criminals deployed deepfake and voice-cloning technology to create fraudulent identities of trusted professionals, particularly immigration attorneys. The scams operated on social media and through voice communications, where the absence of identity verification allowed victims to send money to criminals posing as licensed practitioners. Catching this would have required either platform-level detection of inauthentic media, or victim-side verification through independent contact with the real professional.

The failure was in the deployment of generative AI tools with no inherent safeguards against misuse for impersonation. The scammers used publicly available information from social media to research relationships and construct convincing false personas. It is not established whether the platforms hosting the impersonations had detection systems in place, or what technical measures could reliably distinguish the deepfakes from authentic communications at the point of victim contact.

summary:
Scammers are increasingly using artificial intelligence technology to create deepfakes and clone voices to commit fraud across Georgia and South Florida. The FBI reported that Americans lost nearly $893 million to AI-enabled scams in 2025, with criminals using the technology to impersonate trusted individuals and manipulate victims. Notable cases include a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice and identity were stolen to target immigrants, and a Cobb County couple who lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam.

Florida and Georgia have been particularly affected, with Florida reporting 350 AI-related complaints totaling nearly $39.9 million in losses and Georgia reporting 71 complaints with over $10.4 million in losses. Scammers use generative AI to clone voices from social media, create fake photographs, and research personal relationships to make their schemes more convincing. To protect themselves, authorities recommend families establish code words to verify identities, verify urgent requests through known phone numbers, and avoid sending money based solely on phone calls or voicemails.
